first.rationale: Verify the two most decision-relevant competing beliefs: promotional pricing addresses the immediate SMB threat but its durable-memory summary does not establish retention or long-term customer quality, while shorter onboarding directly addresses the completion and activation declines but only establishes early adoption. Provisionally favor a guarded onboarding simplification test because it targets both deteriorating funnel metrics without creating discount-driven downstream value risk.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the self-serve onboarding flow. The verified record directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and supports sustainable value: completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. Prior signup-simplification evidence also supports activation lift. Reject promotional pricing because verification revealed a 12% retention decline despite short-term qualified-revenue gains, conflicting with the long-term qualified-revenue objective. Uncertainty remains about whether historical onboarding effects will replicate in the current cohort, so retain an experimental holdout rather than rolling out broadly.
